Big Question
Today’s Wonder

Ransom chooses the voyage home beside the two men who kidnapped him. What makes a place worth going home to?

✏️ Fix the Sentence
Capitals and a comma
✅ Correct model
When the bell rang, Professor Lovelore closed the book.

The opening words When the bell rang are an adverb clause: it has its own subject and verb, and it tells when. When a clause like this comes first, a comma follows it. Names of particular people and places start with a capital letter. Use the model to fix the sentence below.

🔧 Fix this one
Tap a word to capitalize it. Tap the small circle after a word to add a comma, then a period, then nothing.

Crossing the Bar
Alfred, Lord Tennyson (1889) · Lines 1–4 of 16
Sunset and evening star, And one clear call for me! And may there be no moaning of the bar, When I put out to sea,
evening star: the planet Venus, the first bright “star” after sunset · bar: a sandbank across the mouth of a harbour, where waves break · moaning: the low roar of the sea breaking on the bar · put out to sea: sail out of the harbour into open water
Which moment in Chapter 21 does this stanza fit best?

🔤 Words: Chapter 21
Five of this week’s ten words

Say the meaning first, then tap the card to check.

🙈
obtuseness
tap to flip
obtuseness
Slowness to notice or understand something obvious. “He was now astonished at his obtuseness, and thanked Oyarsa for his protective measures.”
😩
haggard
tap to flip
haggard
Looking exhausted and worn from worry or lack of sleep. “Weston was pale and haggard from a night of calculations.”
🏘️
parochial
tap to flip
parochial
Limited to one small place; narrow in outlook. “He became vividly conscious that his knowledge of Malacandra was minute, local, parochial.”
🧩
smattering
tap to flip
smattering
A small, scattered bit of knowledge. “… a smattering of the language, a few landscapes, some half-understood physics …”
🧳
sojourn
tap to flip
sojourn
A temporary stay in a place. “… the thousand things he had not noticed during his sojourn there.”

🎓 Questions from Professor Lovelore
She asks. You answer.
0 / 3
Professor Lovelore
Here is my first question. The Oyarsa says Ransom is guilty only of “a little fearfulness,” and that the voyage may be his cure. Out in deep heaven, what has changed in him?
Your answer
Professor Lovelore
Next question. When the Earth turns pear-shaped, Weston gives up and Devine takes the controls. What does Lewis want you to notice?
Your answer
Professor Lovelore
Last question. In Chapter 22, why do the narrator and Ransom publish the story as fiction?
Your answer
Professor Lovelore

Good. Look at what happened to the book. For twenty-one chapters you were inside Ransom’s adventure. Then a new voice said “I” and stood outside it, telling you how the story came to be written.

A story set inside another story is a frame narrative. Lewis’s frame asks you to take the adventure a little more seriously, and it turns the ending into a beginning.

Back to the ship, one entry at a time.

🎭 Remove the Mask
Chapter 22 and the Postscript
Sort each statement: is it part of the story, part of the frame, or something the book never says?
Ransom asks for a pint of bitter in a village inn. The Oyarsa says the eldila will guard the ship. ‘Ransom’ is not the man’s real name. The narrator wrote to Ransom about a word in Bernardus Silvestris. ‘Weston’ is a made-up name for a real professor. Ransom complains that the part about the Malacandrian language was cut down. The narrator saw the space-ship land with his own eyes.
The story (Ch. 1 to 21)
The frame (Ch. 22 and the Postscript)
The book never says
